picks.editorial_note: An international team led by TU Wien's Mario Krenn showed in Nature that AI can autonomously propose novel physics experiments that outperform human-designed setups, a striking demonstration of AI as a genuine scientific discovery partner rather than just a tool.
picks.title: Artificial Intelligence Suggests New Physics Experiments

picks.editorial_note: RWTH Aachen's 'HydroGym' reinforcement-learning platform, published in Nature, gives AI agents active control over fluid dynamics with direct applications to energy, transportation, and defense systems.
picks.title: Training AI Agents that Can Actively Control Fluid Dynamics in Energy, Transportation, and Defense | RWTH Aachen University | EN

picks.editorial_note: HKUST's GSCo framework pairs a generalist medical AI with lightweight specialist models to improve precision healthcare, a scalable architecture that could reshape how clinical AI systems are built.
picks.title: Novel AI Framework Unites Generalist and Specialist Models for Precision Healthcare
picks.university: Hong Kong Univ. of Science and Technology

picks.editorial_note: EPFL researchers trained LLMs to express calibrated 'doubt' when proposing experiments, a step toward AI systems that know the limits of their own scientific reasoning and can better guide discovery.
picks.title: An AI capable of doubt can optimize scientific discovery

picks.editorial_note: NSF's $30 million Science and Technology Center, led by Michigan State with Georgia Tech among eight partner institutions, marks a major federal investment in AI-driven turbulence modeling with implications for energy and flight.
picks.title: New Center Seeks to Unlock the Science of Turbulence for Energy, Flight, and Discovery

picks.editorial_note: A $40 million Department of Labor apprenticeship grant, with University of Cincinnati as a partner, signals serious federal investment in building the skilled workforce pipeline AI, semiconductor, and nuclear industries will need.
picks.title: Major grant expands apprenticeship opportunities at UC

picks.editorial_note: A $2.88 million DOE award to a University of Houston-led coalition applies AI to a strategic national security problem: reducing reliance on foreign-controlled critical mineral and rare-earth magnet supply chains.
picks.title: Department of Energy Awards UH-led Team $2.88M to Use AI to Strengthen America’s Critical Mineral Supply Chain | University of Houston

picks.editorial_note: A $7.7 million partnership between University of Kansas engineers, the Army Corps of Engineers, and DHS is deploying AI-integrated digital twins to improve inspection of aging American dams, a direct application of AI to critical infrastructure safety.
picks.title: Four years later KU researchers continue their work strengthening American dams

picks.editorial_note: UT Austin's new fusion energy seed grants tie into DOE's Genesis Mission, which funds using AI to accelerate fusion research, reflecting growing federal-academic coordination around AI for energy breakthroughs.
picks.title: Fusion Energy Seed Grants Launch New Interdisciplinary Collaborations at UT Austin - UT News
picks.university: The University of Texas at Austin

picks.editorial_note: Federal agency AHRQ's cancellation of dozens of healthcare research grants, including a Johns Hopkins AI project aimed at speeding lung cancer diagnosis, illustrates how shifting federal funding priorities are directly disrupting AI-driven medical research.
picks.title: Funding cuts hit research focused on making American healthcare safer, more efficient
